Algerian Unrest Disrupts Key Sectors as Power and Gas Supplies Falter

Algeria is facing mounting economic disruption as widespread protests and political turmoil enter their second week, with major sectors reporting severe operational difficulties. The unrest, triggered by a disputed parliamentary vote, has led to road blockades, strikes, and intermittent violence in several cities, including Algiers, Oran, and Constantine.

Among the companies hit hardest is Societe Algerienne de L'Electricite et du Gaz SpA, the nation’s largest electricity and gas provider. The company announced on Wednesday that supply interruptions had affected industrial zones in the north and power rationing was implemented in several urban districts. “Our field teams are working around the clock, but access to some sites is limited by road closures and security concerns,” said company spokesperson Nadir Bouzid. “We urge all citizens to conserve energy while we restore normal service.”

The crisis has rippled across the economy. The Algerian Union of Exporters reported that cross-border trade slowed by nearly 40% this week, with shipments delayed at the ports of Annaba and Mostaganem. “Exporters are anxious, as power cuts disrupt cold storage and customs operations,” said union president Samira Zekri.

Local analyst Amine Belkacem warned that continued instability could deter foreign investment and further strain Algeria’s finances. “Energy is the backbone of the Algerian economy. Any interruption has cascading effects on manufacturing, agriculture, and public services,” he said.

Government officials have appealed for calm and pledged to open dialogue with opposition groups, but as of Thursday, major highways remain blocked and sporadic demonstrations continue. Authorities have not provided a timeline for when services will fully resume.
